To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal temperature for fast charging is different depending on the SOC and the charging current and that the frequency of the pulse discharging current has to be optimized to prevent lithium plating.
a health aware fast charging is possible by combining optimal constant current, optimal pulse current and optimal temperature.

the optimal charging current and temperature are determined using the nonlinear model predictive control based on the reduced order electrochemical models and then a pulse discharging current with optimized amplitude and frequency is added to promote lithium stripping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reduction of the charging time while suppressing the degradation of the battery.

the development of a health aware fast charging protocol for lithium ion battery that is based on the combination of CC/CV and pulse discharging charging methods, where the temperature is actively controlled to reduce side reactions and lithium plating, and pulse discharging is added to promote lithium stripping.

the reduction of charging time while suppressing degradation of battery, which is the main cause of battery failure in electric vehicles and renewable energy storage systems, by combining the fast charging protocol and the health aware control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method reduces charging time by 50% compared to CC/CV charging while maintaining similar degradation rate.
the proposed method is capable of reducing charging time while suppressing degradation compared to CC/CV charging protocol.
the proposed method is a good alternative for fast charging method that can reduce charging time and suppress degradation at the same time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed method can charge a large format battery at a high current rate without any capacity fade and the proposed model is a good tool for designing optimal charging methods for lithium ion battery.
the proposed method can be used to achieve a fast charging method with a comparable capacity fade rate to that of CC/CV method.

the proposed charging method reduces the charging time up to 80%, which is comparable to the 1 C constant current charging method, and also suppresses the capacity fade up to 10%, which is comparable with the CC/CV charging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fast charging method that is actively temperature controlled using a nonlinear model predictive controller can significantly reduce charging time while suppressing degradation.
the proposed health aware fast charging protocol can reduce charging time by 61% while keeping the degradation rate comparable to that of the 1 C charging protocol.
the fast charging method proposed in this paper can significantly reduce charging time while suppressing degradation.
